text: Write nested loops over a jagged array, using each row's own length. Fill in the three blanks.
choices: int[][] jag = ___;                  // three rows, lengths not yet fixed
for (int c = 0; c < ___; c++)   // this row's length, not the first row's
explanation: Verified: it prints `[0]`, `[0, 1]`, then `[0, 1, 2]` — three rows of different lengths. Writing `jag[0].length` for the inner bound is the bug this question exists to prevent: it works on rectangular data and throws on the first ragged row. Java has no true two-dimensional array — only arrays of arrays — so ragged is the general case and rectangular is a special one you happen to have built.
